answer: Each identity must bind itself to one hardware security chip (TPM) that signs an attestation every epoch. A chip is like a timber beam: solid, singular, impossible to split into two load-bearing posts. Its private key signs each challenge with a quill that cannot be copied, proving the same physical device is present, and one chip yields exactly one vote. A farm running a hundred identities needs a hundred chips, bought, powered and kept online; their cost piles up like a dune growing with every fake. Lose the chip, lose the identity; share one chip and all collapse to one vote, stake burned.
